speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and yellowing of the skin and eyes. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any pain or tenderness in your upper right abdomen, or any changes in the color of your urine or stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and recent drug use, are you experiencing any fever, nausea, or dark-colored urine? I would like to check for signs of acute hepatitis or other infections.

text: With normal hepatitis serology but severe liver injury and coagulopathy, I need to rule out other causes. Have you recently taken any over-the-counter medications, specifically acetaminophen (Tylenol), or any new supplements?

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal hepatitis serology and your social alcohol history, are you experiencing any abdominal pain, fever, or nausea that might suggest alcoholic hepatitis or another toxin-induced liver injury? I also need to know if you have been taking any prescription medications or herbal supplements recently.
